payload.claim: The spec's Context and Notes sections cite specific saffron/cli.py line numbers to point at the code they mean (watch_parser.error at :272/:274; _stack_admission_shares(args.budget) at :1984-1985; where _stack_end_review/_stack_follow_ups/_stack_finish are built at :2116/:2139/:2148; the end_review=/follow_ups=/finish= keywords at :2198/:2203/:2205; and _stack_end_review's except Exception at :869). At this base commit every one of these is wrong, by a consistent offset (the watch_parser.error pair off by 7 lines, the rest off by 16 lines), because SA-0300 (already landed and reviewed at this base) added a new saffron next-id command and roughly 56 lines to saffron/cli.py, shifting everything after it. The actual lines are 279/281, 2000-2001, 2132/2155/2164, 2214/2219/2221, and 885 respectively (all verified by grep). The substantive claims attached to these citations, what calls what, the ordering, that each callable stays None until the scan resolves, are all independently true in content; only the line pointers are stale. By contrast every tests/test_cli.py line citation checked (:5918, :6915, :6942, :6998, :8503) is exactly correct. Since Claude Code's edit tooling matches by surrounding text rather than line number, this is unlikely to cause a wrong build.
